```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Jeong_2022_nafamostat")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.12793/tcp.2022.30.e20>
  (open access, <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9810492/>)

# What this model is, and what it is not

Jeong 2022 builds a Simcyp (version 21) physiologically based
pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of nafamostat, an intravenous serine-protease
inhibitor that is hydrolysed rapidly by plasma and tissue esterases. The model
is verified against 2-h intravenous infusions of 10, 20 and 40 mg in healthy
Chinese volunteers (Cao et al. 2008, reference 22). It is then applied to two
continuous-infusion regimens proposed for COVID-19: 200 mg/24 h and
4.8 mg/kg/24 h, each for 13 days. For both regimens the paper predicts the
total and unbound plasma concentrations and the total lung-tissue
concentration.

Simcyp's whole-body equations are proprietary and do not appear in the paper.
Distribution uses the full-PBPK layout, with Rodgers and Rowland partition
coefficients multiplied by an estimated `Kp` scalar of 2.18. Elimination is
built from CES2 enzyme kinetics, a plasma esterase half-life, additional liver
microsomal and cytosolic intrinsic clearances, renal clearance and an
additional systemic clearance (Table 1). Converting those inputs into a
systemic clearance needs unpublished Simcyp system values: microsomal and
cytosolic protein per gram of liver, liver weight and plasma volume. The
organ volumes, blood flows and per-tissue `Kp` values are not printed either.
The platform model itself therefore cannot be encoded.

The paper does publish enough output to determine an intravenous reduction:

* **Table 2** gives the PBPK model's predicted mean AUC0-inf at three doses.
  Dose / AUC0-inf is 220.8 L/h at every dose, so this is the model's
  clearance, and nafamostat is dose-linear over 10-40 mg (the CES2 `Km` of
  1,790 uM is far above any plasma concentration).
* **Table 1** gives the predicted steady-state volume, 11.66 L/kg.
* **Figure 1** plots the predicted mean plasma profile for each dose over 8 h.
  The figures in the article PDF are vector graphics, so the curves were read
  from their path coordinates rather than by eye. The digitised apexes
  reproduce the Table 2 predicted Cmax (18.5, 36.9 and 73.9 ng/mL) to within
  0.6%.
* **Figure 2** plots the predicted total plasma, unbound plasma and lung
  profiles over the 13-day infusions.

The reduction fixes clearance at 220.8 L/h and the total volume at
11.66 L/kg x 70 kg. It recovers the remaining distribution constants from
Figure 1 alone and holds out Table 2's Cmax and AUC0-last and all of Figure 2
as independent checks.

# Population

```{r population}
p <- ui$population
pop_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Field = c("Species", "Virtual subjects", "Age", "% female", "Population",
            "Doses"),
  Value = c(p$species, p$n_subjects, p$age_range, p$sex_female_pct,
            p$race_ethnicity, p$dose_range)
)
knitr::kable(pop_tab, caption = "Simulated population (Jeong 2022 Methods).")
```

The clinical verification study (Cao et al. 2008) enrolled 10 healthy Chinese
volunteers per dose, aged 20-30 years, with the sex ratio not reported. The
simulations used 10 virtual trials of 100 subjects aged 20-40 years with a
50:50 sex ratio. No body weight is reported for either the clinical or the
virtual population.

# Source trace

Every value in the `ini()` block, with its source location.

```{r source-trace}
trace_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Parameter, ~Value,       ~Source,
  "lcl",      "220.8 L/h",  "Table 2 predicted AUC0-inf: 10 mg / 45.30, 20 mg / 90.60, 40 mg / 181.00 ng*h/mL",
  "lvc",      "7.61 L",     "Recovered from the Figure 1 predicted mean curves (joint fit, three doses)",
  "lq",       "104 L/h",    "Recovered from Figure 1",
  "lvp",      "42.2 L",     "Recovered from Figure 1",
  "lq2",      "64.8 L/h",   "Recovered from Figure 1",
  "lvp2",     "232 L",      "Recovered from Figure 1",
  "lq3",      "7.57 L/h",   "Recovered from Figure 1",
  "lvp3",     "534.4 L",    "Table 1 'Vss (L/kg)' 11.66 x 70 kg = 816.2 L, minus vc + vp + vp2",
  "fu",       "0.46",       "Table 1 'fu' (predicted in Simcyp)",
  "lkp_lung", "5.44",       "Ratio of the Figure 2C lung curve to the Figure 2A plasma curve",
  "propSd",   "0 (fixed)",  "No residual-error model is reported anywhere in the source"
)
knitr::kable(trace_tab, caption = "Source trace for every fixed parameter.")
```

The model equations are the standard four-compartment mammillary intravenous
system. The outputs are `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` (mg/L to ng/mL), the
unbound concentration `Cu = fu * Cc`, and the lung-tissue concentration
`Clung = kp_lung * Cc`. Both of the last two are algebraic: the unbound
fraction is a constant in the source (Table 1), and Figure 2 shows the lung
concentration at a constant 5.440 times plasma at every plotted time in both
regimens. The lung receives the whole cardiac output and is
perfusion-limited, so it equilibrates with plasma within minutes.

```{r derivation-gate}
theta <- ui$theta
cl_mod  <- exp(theta[["lcl"]])
vss_mod <- exp(theta[["lvc"]]) + exp(theta[["lvp"]]) + exp(theta[["lvp2"]]) +
  exp(theta[["lvp3"]])
auc_inf_pred <- c(`10` = 45.30, `20` = 90.60, `40` = 181.00)  # Table 2
cl_implied <- 1000 * c(10, 20, 40) / auc_inf_pred
stopifnot(
  max(abs(cl_implied / cl_mod - 1)) < 0.001,
  abs(vss_mod / (11.66 * 70) - 1) < 0.001,
  theta[["fu"]] == 0.46
)
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(Dose_mg = c(10, 20, 40), AUCinf = auc_inf_pred,
                 CL_implied = round(cl_implied, 2)) |>
    dplyr::rename("Dose (mg)" = Dose_mg,
                  "Predicted AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)" = AUCinf,
                  "Dose / AUC0-inf (L/h)" = CL_implied),
  caption = "Clearance implied by the Table 2 predictions."
)
```

# Digitised reference curves

The predicted mean curves of Figures 1 and 2, read from the vector paths of
the article PDF. Figure 1 is on a log axis (0.1-100 or 0.1-1,000 ng/mL over
0-8 h); Figure 2 is on linear nM axes with a break between days 2 and 8.
On Figure 2's day-scale axis the first 1.5 h of infusion spans less than two
points of drawing width, so the rise is not resolvable there and the reference
points start at 3 h.

```{r reference-data}
mw <- 347.378  # g/mol, Table 1

fig1_t <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.05, 2.1, 2.25, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)
fig1_ref <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(dose = 10, time = fig1_t, Cc_ref = c(
    14.051, 15.685, 16.994, 17.845, 18.475, 7.032, 5.934, 4.449, 3.306,
    2.207, 1.377, 0.987, 0.769, 0.634, 0.540)),
  tibble::tibble(dose = 20, time = fig1_t, Cc_ref = c(
    28.657, 31.467, 34.028, 35.722, 36.949, 13.537, 11.596, 8.771, 6.547,
    4.386, 2.743, 1.967, 1.535, 1.266, 1.079)),
  tibble::tibble(dose = 40, time = fig1_t, Cc_ref = c(
    56.496, 62.151, 67.737, 71.061, 73.552, 27.765, 23.729, 17.515, 13.006,
    8.821, 5.421, 3.937, 3.073, 2.509, 2.138))
)

fig2_t <- c(3, 6, 9, 13, 18, 24, 31, 39, 48, 192, 312)
fig2_ref <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(regimen = "200 mg/24 h", output = "Total plasma", time = fig2_t,
                 nM_ref = c(92.9, 98.6, 102.4, 105.7, 108.3, 110.2, 111.4, 112.2, 112.6, 113.0, 113.1)),
  tibble::tibble(regimen = "200 mg/24 h", output = "Unbound plasma", time = fig2_t,
                 nM_ref = c(42.1, 44.7, 46.4, 47.9, 49.1, 49.9, 50.5, 50.8, 51.0, 51.2, 51.2)),
  tibble::tibble(regimen = "200 mg/24 h", output = "Lung tissue", time = fig2_t,
                 nM_ref = c(505.5, 536.3, 557.2, 575.0, 589.1, 599.3, 606.1, 610.2, 612.4, 614.7, 615.3)),
  tibble::tibble(regimen = "4.8 mg/kg/24 h", output = "Total plasma", time = fig2_t,
                 nM_ref = c(136.1, 144.6, 150.2, 154.9, 158.6, 161.3, 163.3, 164.6, 165.5, 166.1, 166.3)),
  tibble::tibble(regimen = "4.8 mg/kg/24 h", output = "Unbound plasma", time = fig2_t,
                 nM_ref = c(61.9, 65.7, 68.2, 70.4, 72.1, 73.4, 74.3, 74.8, 75.1, 75.6, 75.7)),
  tibble::tibble(regimen = "4.8 mg/kg/24 h", output = "Lung tissue", time = fig2_t,
                 nM_ref = c(743.7, 789.0, 819.8, 846.0, 866.7, 881.7, 891.8, 897.8, 901.1, 904.6, 905.5))
)
```

## Why four compartments

After each 2-h infusion the Figure 1 curves drop about 60% within three
minutes, then fall with half-lives near 0.4 h and 3 h. The 11.66 L/kg volume
also needs a deep, slowly equilibrating space. With clearance and Vss held at
the same two anchors, the best two- and three-compartment reductions miss
Figure 1 with log-scale RMSE of 0.37 and 0.085, against 0.050 here. They miss
the 10 mg Table 2 Cmax by -14% and -10%; this model misses it by -0.6%. The
four-compartment model's half-lives follow.

```{r half-lives}
k <- with(as.list(exp(theta[c("lcl", "lvc", "lq", "lvp", "lq2", "lvp2",
                              "lq3", "lvp3")])),
          c(kel = lcl / lvc, k12 = lq / lvc, k21 = lq / lvp,
            k13 = lq2 / lvc, k31 = lq2 / lvp2, k14 = lq3 / lvc,
            k41 = lq3 / lvp3))
A <- with(as.list(k), rbind(
  c(-(kel + k12 + k13 + k14), k21, k31, k41),
  c(k12, -k21, 0, 0),
  c(k13, 0, -k31, 0),
  c(k14, 0, 0, -k41)
))
thalf <- sort(log(2) / -Re(eigen(A)$values))
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(Phase = 1:4, `Half-life (h)` = signif(thalf, 3)),
             caption = "Disposition half-lives of the reduction.")
```

The terminal half-life of about 50 h belongs to the deep compartment that
carries most of the 816 L Vss. It holds little of a 2-h dose. AUC beyond 8 h
is about 8% of AUC0-inf, which matches Table 2, where AUC0-last is 92% of
AUC0-inf at every dose. That deep compartment also drives the slow approach to
plateau over the first two days of the Figure 2 infusions.

# Virtual cohort

The model has no random effects, so it is deterministic. One subject per
regimen fully describes each arm.

* **Verification arms**: 10, 20 and 40 mg as 2-h infusions, observed to 14
  days so that PKNCA can estimate AUC0-inf.
* **COVID-19 arms**: 200 mg/24 h and 4.8 mg/kg/24 h for 13 days. The paper
  does not print the body weight behind the per-kilogram regimen. Because
  this reduction has an absolute clearance, the ratio of the two Figure 2
  plateaus (166.3 / 113.1 = 1.470) fixes the implied daily dose at
  1.470 x 200 mg = 294 mg, or 4.8 mg/kg at 61.3 kg. That weight is used only
  to convert this regimen into an infusion rate.

Observations are placed on the `central` ODE state; `Cc`, `Cu` and `Clung` are
returned as algebraic outputs on those rows.

```{r cohort}
wt_covid <- 1.470 * 200 / 4.8   # kg, from the Figure 2 plateau ratio

regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,              ~dose_mg,           ~dur_h,  ~t_end,
  "10 mg over 2 h",  10,                 2,       336,
  "20 mg over 2 h",  20,                 2,       336,
  "40 mg over 2 h",  40,                 2,       336,
  "200 mg/24 h",     200 * 13,           24 * 13, 24 * 13,
  "4.8 mg/kg/24 h",  4.8 * wt_covid * 13, 24 * 13, 24 * 13
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

make_infusion <- function(id, arm, dose_mg, dur_h, t_end) {
  obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(
    seq(0, 3, by = 0.01), seq(3, 48, by = 0.25), seq(48, t_end, by = 2),
    fig1_t, fig2_t[fig2_t <= t_end], t_end
  )))
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(id = id, time = 0, amt = dose_mg, rate = dose_mg / dur_h,
                   evid = 1L, cmt = "central", arm = arm),
    tibble::tibble(id = id, time = obs_grid, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_,
                   evid = 0L, cmt = "central", arm = arm)
  )
}

events <- regimens |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(make_infusion(id, arm, dose_mg, dur_h, t_end)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]),
          sum(events$evid == 1L) == 5L)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "arm",
                       rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = round(time, 6))

stopifnot(all(is.finite(sim$Cc)), all(sim$Cc >= 0))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1: 2-h infusions of 10, 20 and 40 mg

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.2}
sim_f1 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(arm %in% c("10 mg over 2 h", "20 mg over 2 h",
                           "40 mg over 2 h"), time <= 8) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose = as.numeric(sub(" mg.*", "", arm)))

ggplot(sim_f1, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = fig1_ref, aes(time, Cc_ref), shape = 1, size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ dose, labeller = labeller(dose = \(x) paste(x, "mg"))) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1000)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma nafamostat (ng/mL)",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 1A-C of Jeong 2022.",
                       "Line: reduction. Circles: published PBPK predicted mean.")) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r figure-1-gate}
f1_cmp <- fig1_ref |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = paste(dose, "mg over 2 h"), time = round(time, 6)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim |> dplyr::select(arm, time, Cc), by = c("arm", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (Cc / Cc_ref - 1))
stopifnot(!anyNA(f1_cmp$Cc))
# These points were fitted, so this measures the quality of the reduction,
# not an independent validation. Median and 90th percentile, not the extreme:
# the curves are steep around the end of infusion, where a sub-point error in
# reading time moves the concentration most.
stopifnot(abs(median(f1_cmp$pct)) < 5,
          quantile(abs(f1_cmp$pct), 0.9) < 10)
knitr::kable(
  f1_cmp |>
    dplyr::group_by(dose) |>
    dplyr::summarise(median_pct = round(median(pct), 1),
                     max_abs_pct = round(max(abs(pct)), 1)) |>
    dplyr::rename("Dose (mg)" = dose, "Median % diff" = median_pct,
                  "Max |% diff|" = max_abs_pct),
  caption = "Reduction vs. the Figure 1 predicted mean curves (fitted points)."
)
```

## Figure 2: 13-day continuous infusions (held out)

None of these points was used to build the model.

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
sim_f2 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(arm %in% c("200 mg/24 h", "4.8 mg/kg/24 h")) |>
  dplyr::transmute(regimen = arm, time,
                   `Total plasma` = Cc / mw * 1000,
                   `Unbound plasma` = Cu / mw * 1000,
                   `Lung tissue` = Clung / mw * 1000) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(regimen, time), names_to = "output",
                      values_to = "nM") |>
  dplyr::mutate(output = factor(output, c("Total plasma", "Unbound plasma",
                                          "Lung tissue")))

ggplot(sim_f2, aes(time / 24, nM)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 30, ymax = 240,
           fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = fig2_ref |>
               dplyr::mutate(output = factor(output, levels(sim_f2$output))),
             aes(time / 24, nM_ref), shape = 1, size = 1.6) +
  facet_grid(regimen ~ output) +
  labs(x = "Days", y = "Nafamostat (nM)",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 2A-F of Jeong 2022. Band: proposed",
                       "therapeutic range 30-240 nM; dashed: in vitro IC50",
                       "about 10 nM.\nCircles: published PBPK predicted mean.")) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r figure-2-gate}
f2_cmp <- fig2_ref |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_f2 |> dplyr::mutate(output = as.character(output)),
                   by = c("regimen", "output", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (nM / nM_ref - 1))
stopifnot(!anyNA(f2_cmp$nM))
# Structural check: a wrong clearance, volume or unit conversion moves the
# whole profile by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(median(f2_cmp$pct)) < 5,
          quantile(abs(f2_cmp$pct), 0.9) < 8)
knitr::kable(
  f2_cmp |>
    dplyr::group_by(regimen, output) |>
    dplyr::summarise(median_pct = round(median(pct), 1),
                     max_abs_pct = round(max(abs(pct)), 1),
                     .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen, "Output" = output,
                  "Median % diff" = median_pct, "Max |% diff|" = max_abs_pct),
  caption = "Reduction vs. the Figure 2 predicted mean curves (held out)."
)
```

The total plasma plateau runs about 4% below the figure for both regimens.
Steady state is `rate / CL`, so the figure implies a clearance of about
212 L/h, against the 220.8 L/h implied by Table 2. The two published outputs
of the same platform model disagree by that amount, and the reduction follows
Table 2. The unbound comparison sits about 1.5 percentage points closer to
the figure than the total-plasma comparison, because the printed fu of 0.46 is
slightly above the 0.453 ratio of the plotted curves. Both regimens hold the total and unbound plasma concentrations
inside the proposed 30-240 nM range, and the lung concentration far above the
10 nM IC50, which is the paper's conclusion.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sd_arms <- c("10 mg over 2 h", "20 mg over 2 h", "40 mg over 2 h")
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(arm %in% sd_arms, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L, arm %in% sd_arms) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dur_h = 2)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | arm + id,
                             concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id,
                             doseu = "mg", route = "intravascular",
                             duration = "dur_h")

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0),
  end = c(8, Inf),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)

nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                      intervals = intervals))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs",
                                "half.life")) |>
  # PKNCA also reports tmax on the open-ended interval, where it is only an
  # intermediate of the half-life fit.
  dplyr::filter(!(PPTESTCD == "tmax" & is.infinite(end)))
stopifnot(nrow(nca_df) == 15L, all(is.finite(nca_df$PPORRES)))

knitr::kable(
  nca_df |>
    dplyr::mutate(PPORRES = signif(PPORRES, 4)) |>
    dplyr::select(arm, start, end, PPTESTCD, PPORRES),
  caption = "PKNCA results for the three simulated 2-h infusions."
)
```

`AUC0-inf = dose / CL` holds exactly for any linear model with a single dose,
which checks the NCA setup as much as the model:

```{r closed-form-gate}
aucinf_nca <- nca_df |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs")
aucinf_closed <- 1000 * c(10, 20, 40) / cl_mod
stopifnot(max(abs(aucinf_nca$PPORRES[match(sd_arms, aucinf_nca$arm)] /
                    aucinf_closed - 1)) < 0.01)
```

# Comparison against the published NCA

## Against the paper's own PBPK predictions

AUC0-last is taken over 0-8 h, the span of the observed sampling in Figure 1.
Cmax and AUC0-last were not used to build the model; AUC0-inf was, through
the clearance, and is shown for completeness.

```{r nca-compare-pred}
published_pred <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,             ~cmax, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs,
  "10 mg over 2 h", 18.50,   41.70,   45.30,
  "20 mg over 2 h", 36.90,   83.50,   90.60,
  "40 mg over 2 h", 73.90,  167.00,  181.00
)

cmp_pred <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_df |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast",
                                                       "aucinf.obs")),
  reference = published_pred,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_pred,
  caption = paste("Reduction vs. the Simcyp predicted means in Jeong 2022",
                  "Table 2. * differs by >20%."),
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r")
)

pct_pred <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.eE+-]", "", as.character(cmp_pred[["% diff"]])))
)
stopifnot(sum(is.finite(pct_pred)) == 9L,
          max(abs(pct_pred), na.rm = TRUE) < 5)
```

## Against the observed data

Table 2 also reports the observed means from Cao et al. 2008 (n = 10 per
dose). The PBPK model overpredicts the observed AUC by 1.5-1.7-fold, which
the paper discusses and attributes to high variability in the observed data
and nafamostat's instability in samples. The reduction inherits that
overprediction because it reproduces the platform model.

```{r nca-compare-obs}
published_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,             ~cmax, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs,
  "10 mg over 2 h", 14.50,   24.00,   27.60,
  "20 mg over 2 h", 40.40,   56.40,   59.50,
  "40 mg over 2 h", 60.40,  110.00,  115.00
)

cmp_obs <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_df |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast",
                                                       "aucinf.obs")),
  reference = published_obs,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_obs,
  caption = paste("Reduction vs. the observed means in Jeong 2022 Table 2",
                  "(Cao et al. 2008). * differs by >20%."),
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

The starred rows are the platform model's own overprediction (the paper's
Table 2 ratios are 1.48-1.74 for AUC), not a defect of the reduction.

# Assumptions and deviations

1. **This is a reduction of a platform model, recovered partly from its
   published output curves.** Clearance (from Table 2), Vss (Table 1) and fu
   (Table 1) are paper values. The six distribution constants were fitted by
   the maintainers to the Figure 1 predicted mean curves, read from the vector
   paths of the article PDF, by log-scale least squares with clearance and Vss
   held fixed. The lung ratio was read from Figure 2. Everything else was held
   out: Table 2 Cmax and AUC0-last (within 1%) and all six Figure 2 curves
   (within 6%).
2. **Body weight of 70 kg is assumed for the volume.** Table 1 gives Vss in
   L/kg and no body weight appears anywhere in the paper. The 70 kg reference
   is the standing rounded-standard convention. The fit is insensitive to it:
   with Vss at 11.66 L/kg x 61.3 kg (715 L), the Figure 1 fit is essentially
   unchanged. `WT` is recorded in `covariatesDataExcluded` rather than carried
   as a live covariate, because the clearance is an absolute value for the
   unpublished virtual population.
3. **The 4.8 mg/kg/24 h regimen is simulated at 61.3 kg.** That weight is
   back-solved from the ratio of the two Figure 2 plateaus. It is not a model
   parameter; at 70 kg the same regimen would give a plateau 14% higher.
4. **Clearance follows Table 2, not Figure 2.** The Table 2 predicted AUC0-inf
   implies 220.8 L/h, and the Figure 2 plateau implies about 212 L/h. The
   paper does not explain the difference; it may reflect a different virtual
   population for the application simulations. Table 2 is a printed number,
   so it is used.
5. **The printed fu is used for the unbound output.** Table 1 gives 0.46; the
   plotted unbound/total ratio in Figure 2 is 0.453. The printed value raises
   `Cu` by about 1.5% relative to that ratio, which partly offsets the 4%
   clearance gap of item 4; `Cu` runs about 2.5% below Figure 2B/E.
6. **The lung output is a constant ratio.** The Figure 2 lung curves are
   exactly 5.440 times the plasma curves at every plotted time, in both
   regimens. This is the Simcyp-predicted lung `Kp` times the 2.18 `Kp`
   scalar. An algebraic ratio reproduces it; it does not describe lung
   kinetics faster than the perfusion time of the lung (minutes).
7. **The global sensitivity analysis is not reproducible.** Figure 3 ranks
   physiological inputs (haematocrit, plasma volume scalar, microsomal
   protein, cardiac output) that exist only inside the platform model.
8. **Doses are nominal.** The paper does not say whether the 10-40 mg doses
   refer to nafamostat or to nafamostat mesylate. The reduction reproduces the
   platform's output at the nominal dose and inherits whatever convention the
   platform used, with a molecular weight of 347.378 g/mol (Table 1).
9. **No inter-individual variability and no residual error.** Jeong 2022 is a
   PBPK simulation study, not a population-PK fit. Its 5th-95th percentile
   bands are the spread of a Simcyp virtual population, not estimated
   variance components. The model has no etas and `propSd` is fixed at zero.
10. **No errata were found.** A EuropePMC search on 2026-10-10 (comment and
    correction links, and a correction/erratum keyword search) found no
    correction notice for doi:10.12793/tcp.2022.30.e20.
